name: spanlo
concept: Context spanning visits and center workflows
prompt: Use case: logo-brand. Create a carefully art-directed original software identity proof for a real learning-center operations application. The product combines attendance/QR check-in, instructor handoffs per subject, material preparation, observations, skills and academic progress, visit history and center analytics. Its defining value is preserving student context as staff coordinate the center. The user has rejected arbitrary pleasant colors, car-brand monograms, pet-food blobs, hotel serif/leaf marks, vape-store lettering and granola-bird illustrations. Design a cohesive NAME + SYMBOL concept whose structure comes from the actual product idea. This must clearly feel like a useful contemporary software product for adult staff, with warmth through readability and proportion. White or cool neutral background, flat vector-style graphics, precise kerning, distinctive but restrained humanist sans-serif lettering. Avoid chunky bubble fonts, luxury serifs, slanted sports type, automotive initials, shields, mascots, animals, plants, flowers, food, sparkles, generic chat bubbles, infinity loops, gears, metallic effects, bevels, shadows, gradients and photographic mockups. Do not imitate any existing company's mark. Make one elegant uncomplicated primary logo with no surrounding badge. The main logo must dominate the top half. Lower half contains one restrained realistic staff-interface corner showing that same logo at small size, then only the real navigation labels 'Home', 'Student Roster', 'Homework Preparation', 'Center Activity'. No fabricated student records, numbers, product features or giant decorative cards. Include a small standalone one-color symbol as a proof. Keep every repeated symbol structurally identical. The only other text is the brief supplied concept caption. Landscape 3:2, ample clean margins. Exact brand name 'spanlo', lowercase s-p-a-n-l-o. Concept caption exactly 'Connected across every visit.' The name is coined from span. The mark must make the same idea visible: two clean open rectangular record frames offset slightly, held together by a single continuous connecting stroke spanning the space between them. A clear common line and open negative space communicate that the same student context carries through separate records. NOT a literal S, chain, highway, bridge illustration, folder icon or pair of chat bubbles. At most three thick simple geometric elements with gently rounded terminals. Give the small silhouette a distinctive offset and a memorable large open counter. Color system: graphite #262735 wordmark, persimmon-orange #F06736 symbol, very light cool gray #F6F7FB interface, a restrained lavender #ABB1F4 secondary accent only inside the UI. Absolutely no cream, leaves, cereal-brand colors or a blue automotive logo. Typography: lowercase humanist sans, medium-semibold, clear double-storey a, a notably open o and generous comfortable letter spacing; mature and approachable, not thick bubbly display. App corner has an orange active Home marker, graphite navigation text, a small lavender highlight used sparingly. Main horizontal lockup should have perfect mark/wordmark balance and feel intentional even in black and white. This is the lead product-grounded concept.

name: rellin
concept: Relay and line: carrying work and context between staff

Avoid chunky bubble fonts, luxury serifs, slanted sports type, automotive initials, shields, mascots, animals, plants, flowers, food, sparkles, generic chat bubbles, infinity loops, gears, metallic effects, bevels, shadows, gradients and photographic mockups. The coined name is inspired by relay and line. The logo mark must express a handoff: two open bracket-like receiving forms face one another around a single shared small rectangular context tile, one form slightly higher than the other. The shared tile is the visual focus; preserve clean open gaps and a distinctive compact silhouette using at most three elements. Typography: a thoughtfully spaced upright sans-serif with slightly narrower proportions than standard geometric branding, firm flat terminals and comfortable readable weight, a distinctive l-l rhythm; no italic, slab serif, retro display or bubble letters. In the small staff-interface corner, use a slender teal active-navigation bar and understated white surfaces; the name and handoff mark must still read as one coherent identity. The one-color proof must retain the shared-tile idea with open space, without needing its blue color.
